description: Mechanical verification registry for this workspace. Each entry names a file and a pattern, and says whether that pattern is expected to be present or absent; scripts/verify_issues.py decides whether the claim still holds. Identifiers are local to this repository and do not correspond to identifiers in any other one. A pattern is matched line by line with Python's re, so it must match within a single line: a string spanning adjacent source literals that the interpreter joins cannot be pinned, because no line contains it.

issues.title: Stream cancellation refuses the string request IDs JSON-RPC permits
issues.description: _handle_mgp_cancel accepts params.request_id only when it is an int and answers invalid-params otherwise. JSON-RPC 2.0 defines an id as a String, Number or NULL, and this package's own helpers already type request ids as int or str: write_mgp_method_response and write_mgp_stream_chunk both accept either. The gap handler repeats the same integer-only test. A client that follows the specification and numbers its requests with strings can therefore never cancel a stream -- the cancel is answered as malformed even while a stream is registered under that exact id, so the stream runs to completion and the client is told it asked wrongly.
issues.measured: _handle_mgp_cancel driven with request_id 'req-abc' while the active-stream map held that key: the reply was error -32602 'params.request_id must be an integer', and the registered stream was never signalled.

issues.title: Servers advertise the streaming extension while streaming is disabled
issues.description: _build_mgp_capabilities declares the streaming extension unconditionally, but ProviderConfig.supports_streaming defaults to False and the call handler enters the streaming path only when that flag is true. The declaration is what a peer negotiates on, so a peer reading it asks for chunks this server will never emit. The declaration should follow the flag it claims to describe.
issues.measured: A ProviderConfig with supports_streaming False produced extensions ['permissions', 'streaming'].

issues.title: A malformed stream line is discarded and the answer is still reported complete
issues.description: The event-stream reader catches a JSON decode error on a data line and continues, so a chunk that fails to parse is dropped with nothing recorded. The only condition that marks a response as truncated is the absence of the terminating sentinel, so a stream that loses a line in the middle and then terminates normally is returned as a complete answer. The caller cannot tell a whole reply from one with a hole in it, which is the distinction the completeness guarantee exists to make.
issues.measured: A stream of two good deltas, one unparseable line and the sentinel returned a result containing only the two good deltas, carrying streamed true with chunks_sent 2, with no partial marker and no error.

issues.title: Unparseable tool arguments become an empty argument object
issues.description: parse_chat_think_result decodes a tool call's arguments string and, when the decode fails, substitutes an empty dict and appends the call anyway with no error marker. The caller receives a well-formed tool call whose arguments were invented here. A tool invoked with no arguments can mean something very different from the call the model actually asked for, and nothing downstream can tell the two apart.
issues.measured: A call named 'delete_all' whose arguments string was the unterminated '{"scope": "prod' came back as type tool_calls, name 'delete_all', arguments {}, with no error field on the result.

issues.title: The non-streaming provider path has no receive-size budget
issues.description: call_llm_api issues an ordinary post and then parses the whole body, and the streaming error path reads the body in full before parsing it. Neither declares a content-length ceiling nor counts received bytes, so the peer decides how much memory this process spends.
issues.measured: Against a transport returning a 33.6 MB response the call returned normally with all 33554432 characters intact and a traced peak of 67.1 MB, twice the body, because the raw bytes and the decoded string are live at the same moment. Note the limit of the measurement: the body arrived in one piece, so this establishes that nothing rejects an oversized response, not how a cap would behave against a slow sender.

issues.title: Streaming bounds the retransmit buffer but not the accumulated answer
issues.description: The streaming handler keeps a ring buffer of emitted chunks bounded by _CHUNK_BUFFER_MAX, and that bound is documented. The authoritative result, however, is a single string every text delta is appended to, and it must survive until the stream ends. The loop has no output-byte, token or total-duration budget, and read timeouts measure inactivity between chunks rather than elapsed time, so a peer that keeps emitting small chunks holds the request open and the string grows for as long as it does. The bound that exists is not the one that matters.
issues.measured: With the ring buffer at 100 entries, 4000 deltas accumulated 1024000 characters and a traced peak of 6.2 MB; the documented bound never came into play.

issues.title: Search providers parse the whole upstream body before applying max_results
issues.description: Every provider materialises the complete upstream response before it narrows the result set: the JSON providers parse the whole body and then slice to max_results, and the HTML provider decodes the entire document before extracting entries. max_results bounds what the caller sees, not what this process spends, and a bound applied after parsing is not a bound on the parse.
issues.measured: Against a transport returning a 59.1 MB body of 200000 entries with max_results 3, the call returned 3 results after a traced peak of 173.0 MB -- the body plus the parsed structure.

issues.title: A proxy-only deployment still resolves to a direct external endpoint
issues.description: load_llm_provider_config documents that under proxy-only isolation all outbound HTTP is expected to route through the injected proxy, and it uses that proxy as the default endpoint. An explicit endpoint override still wins, and when the override points outside localhost the loader only logs a warning: it neither refuses the configuration nor rewrites it. The provider then posts agent context straight to that host, leaving the boundary the deployment was built to enforce, with a warning line as the only trace. A warning is the right severity for a misconfiguration; it is not the right severity for silently leaving an isolation boundary.
issues.measured: With the proxy variable set and the endpoint override pointing at an external host, the resolved configuration carried the external URL unchanged.
issues.pattern: if proxy_base and \"127\.0\.0\.1\" not in api_url

issues.title: The semantic cache compares vectors of different widths by truncating to the shorter
issues.description: _dot_product pairs its two operands with zip, which stops at the shorter one, and nothing records or compares the width of a stored vector against the width of a query vector. Embedding width is a property of the model, so any change of model or backend leaves entries of one width being scored against queries of another over whatever prefix they share. The score is then compared against a similarity threshold as though it meant the same thing, and a prefix agreement is enough to clear it. The failure is a cache that answers a question it was never asked.
issues.measured: _dot_product of a 384-dimension unit vector and a 768-dimension unit vector returned 1.0. End to end, an entry stored with a 768-dimension backend was returned as a hit for a semantically unrelated query embedded at 384 dimensions.
issues.pattern: return sum\(x \* y for x, y in zip\(a, b\)\)

issues.title: The semantic cache accepts an embedding response of any size and any width
issues.description: _embed issues an ordinary post, parses the whole JSON body, and takes the first vector, with no response-byte ceiling, no batch-cardinality check and no dimension check. The embedding client in this same package validates its responses; this path does not, so the backend decides how much memory a lookup costs and how wide a cached vector is.
issues.measured: A 28.0 MB response carrying a single 4000000-dimension vector was accepted and cached in full, at a traced peak of 261.5 MB.

issues.title: A non-finite embedding is normalised past the guard and cached
issues.description: _embed computes the vector's norm and divides only when the norm exceeds a small epsilon. A vector containing a non-finite value has a non-finite norm, and every comparison against a non-finite number is false, so the guard is not taken and the values are stored exactly as received. Scoring that entry yields a non-finite similarity, and 'greater than the best so far' is false for it too, so the entry can never win a lookup: it occupies a slot in a bounded cache and can never be returned from it. Nothing between the response and the store rejects the value, and nothing afterwards reports that an entry has become unreachable.
issues.measured: A backend response containing a bare NaN token was accepted by _embed and cached with the value intact; scoring it against a unit vector produced a non-finite similarity, and the subsequent lookup returned no hit.

issues.title: The registry named no schema, so nothing said what its shape was
issues.description: The registry carried no `$schema` field at all, so there was no link from the data to any description of its shape, and the checker asked for none. It did carry a root `version` of "1.0" -- a number nothing compared to anything, and the same value three sibling registries declared for three shapes that had already diverged from this one and from each other. A field the checker does not read cannot be wrong loudly; it can only be wrong quietly, which is what happened in the siblings: one named a file its repository does not contain, and one held a URL that had rotted into a 404, both with their gates green for months.
issues.measured: On 2026-09-08 the registry's root keys were exactly [version, description, issues]; the checker read neither of the first two. Asking the GitHub API for the document a sibling registry's `$schema` URL named returned 404. After the fix, five malformed pointers (absent, a path naming nothing, a URL, an absolute path, and one escaping the repository) each exited 1 where the previous checker exited 0, and a valid pointer exited 0 on both.
issues.pattern: is not a file in this repository

issues.title: Endpoint credentials reached failure evidence and logs in any spelling but the configured one
issues.description: The client removed userinfo and query strings from exception text only by replacing the configured URL string. httpx quotes its own normalised spelling of the request URL (host lower-cased, a default port dropped, userinfo and query percent-encoded), so with any other spelling the password or query key was written to the WARNING log and returned in the failure evidence callers quote. Every URL in the text is now rebuilt without userinfo and query (redact_urls), after the configured spellings are replaced.
issues.measured: With an endpoint configured as http://svc:PASSWORD@LOCALHOST:8401/embed?key=SECRET and a 503 from the server, the failure evidence of embed, capabilities and token counting contained both secrets in httpx's lower-case spelling; five spellings were tested in packages/mcp-common/tests/test_embedding_redaction.py, all 15 cases failing before the change and passing after.

issues.title: httpx's INFO request line logged endpoint credentials on every request
issues.description: httpx logs each request at INFO as 'HTTP Request: POST <url>' with the URL as sent, through its own logger, which none of the client's sanitising reached. A host that logs at INFO wrote a credential configured in the endpoint URL into every line, on success as well as on failure. initialize() now installs a filter on the httpx logger that strips userinfo and query from every URL in the record.
issues.measured: With an endpoint carrying userinfo and a query key, one successful embed through a mock transport produced an httpx INFO record containing both; after the change the record still names the method, host and path and contains neither (test_httpx_request_log_line_carries_no_credential).

issues.title: A deeply nested backend body raised RecursionError out of every failure boundary
issues.pattern: embedding response is nested deeper than the parser can follow
issues.description: The JSON decoder answers nesting deeper than the interpreter's recursion limit with RecursionError. Such a body is a few hundred kilobytes, inside the response byte budget, and RecursionError is in no failure boundary's except tuple, so it escaped embed, capabilities and token counting and aborted the caller's operation instead of reaching it as a failed call. The decode now maps it to EmbeddingResponseError.
issues.measured: A 200 response of 100,000 nested arrays raised RecursionError from embed_with_outcome, capabilities_with_outcome and count_tokens_with_outcome, with and without a response budget; after the change each returns a failed outcome whose error names the nesting.

issues.title: An integral float argument was replaced by the default
issues.description: JSON Schema counts 3.0 as an integer, so a tool whose input schema declares an integer accepts it, but validate_int returned the default for anything that is not a Python int. A client that serialises every number as a float had its count, limit or TTL silently replaced by the default. validate_int now returns int(val) for a float with no fractional part; 2.5, inf and nan still give the default.
issues.measured: validate_int({'k': 3.0}, 'k', 10) returned 10; it now returns the int 3. Reported downstream through a real tools/call handler, where count=3.0 searched at the default of 10.

issues.title: A malformed configured endpoint URL escaped the embedding client's failure boundary
issues.description: Two routes. httpx raises InvalidURL, which is not a RequestError, while building a request to a URL whose port is not a number, and no boundary caught it, so embed, capabilities and token counting raised instead of returning a failed outcome. A port httpx accepts but urlsplit rejects (out of range) reached the request and failed on its own terms, and then _safe_endpoint, called inside the except handler to name the endpoint, raised ValueError in place of the failure it was reporting. InvalidURL is now in the boundaries' except tuple, and _safe_endpoint no longer raises on a bad port.
issues.measured: With http_url http://127.0.0.1:abc/embed (and :443x) each of the three calls raised httpx.InvalidURL; with :99999 and a 503 backend each raised ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535 out of the handler. After the change each returns a failed outcome naming InvalidURL, or the 503 and the endpoint, respectively.

issues.title: A negative cache size made every successful single-text embed raise KeyError
issues.description: _cache_put stored the entry, then evicted while the cache was larger than the size, removing the entry and then popping an empty cache. The KeyError came after the request had succeeded and outside the failure boundary, so embed and embed_with_outcome raised on every single-text call. A negative size is now logged and treated as 0, which already means no caching.
issues.measured: EmbeddingClient(cache_size=-1) raised KeyError: 'dictionary is empty' from embed_with_outcome on a successful response; it now returns the vector on every call, sending each one to the backend.

issues.title: A token no HTTP client can present loaded as a credential
issues.description: resolve_env_token and validate_token_entries checked only that a token is non-empty ASCII. A token with leading or trailing whitespace (a secret written with echo ends in a newline) or a control character loaded, but HTTP strips the whitespace around a header value and cannot carry a control character, so its client got a 401 on every request and nothing named the cause. Both now refuse such a token with a message that names the defect and not the token.
issues.measured: resolve_env_token accepted 'secret-value\n', 'secret-value ', '\tsecret-value' and tokens containing ESC or DEL, directly and through ${ENV}, and validate_token_entries accepted them; each now raises CredentialError, and tokens of ordinary punctuation still load.

issues.title: tool_calls null or object-typed tool arguments turned an answer into an internal error
issues.description: parse_chat_think_result entered the tool-call branch whenever the key was present and iterated message.tool_calls, so a plain answer carrying tool_calls: null raised TypeError, and a non-dict entry or function raised AttributeError. Arguments sent as a JSON object reached json.loads, which raised TypeError because only JSONDecodeError was caught. A tool_calls value that is not a list, and entries or functions that are not objects, are now skipped; object arguments are used as they are, and arguments that are neither string nor object become empty, as unparseable ones already did.
issues.measured: tool_calls None, 5, 'none' and [None, 'x', {'function': None}] raised TypeError or AttributeError; arguments {'q': 'x'} and None raised TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray. Each now returns the final answer or the call with its arguments.

issues.title: A connection dropped mid-stream discarded text already streamed
issues.description: handle_think_with_tools_streaming promises a partial result when a mid-stream error follows at least one chunk, but its inner handler caught only timeouts, refused connections and LlmApiError. A reset (ReadError) or a peer closing a chunked body early (RemoteProtocolError) went to the generic error path, which returned error_code internal with no content although the chunks had already reached the client. The inner handler now catches every httpx.TransportError.
issues.measured: Two content deltas followed by ReadError, or by RemoteProtocolError, returned {'error': ..., 'error_code': 'internal'}; they now return the partial result with content 'half done', chunks_sent 2 and error code stream_error.

issues.title: A cancel sent just after its streaming tools/call was answered not_active and lost
issues.description: The interceptor forwarded a streaming tools/call and answered a cancel from the registered streams as they were at that moment, but the handler registers its stream only after the SDK dispatches the call. A cancel read in that window was answered not_active, nothing remembered it, and the stream ran in full. The interceptor now records a forwarded call the server will stream, keeps a cancel that names it, and the handler applies that cancel as it registers, before any chunk; the entry is dropped when the call ends, and the table is bounded.
issues.measured: Against the code with the record or the hand-over removed, a cancel fed through the interceptor right after its tools/call was answered {'cancelled': False, 'reason': 'not_active'} and the handler then streamed and returned the full answer; with them, the cancel is answered cancelled and the handler returns content '' with chunks_sent 0 and the cancel reason.

issues.title: A DuckDuckGo result without a snippet took the next result's
issues.description: The snippet for each result was searched for in the 2,000 characters after its title anchor, a window not bounded at the next result. When a result had no snippet and the next one's began within the window, the next snippet was attributed to the wrong URL. The window now ends at the next result's title anchor.
issues.measured: A page whose first result has no snippet returned that result with the second result's snippet; it now returns an empty snippet for the first and keeps the second's.

issues.title: A streamed tool-call fragment that is not an object, or has a bad index, dropped the answer
issues.pattern: if not isinstance\(tc_index, int\) or tc_index < 0:
issues.description: The streaming twin of bug-020, found while fixing it. The buffer that assembles streamed tool calls called .get on each fragment and compared its index with the buffer length, so a fragment that is not an object, or an index that is a string or negative, raised and turned the answer into an internal error. Such a fragment is now skipped.
issues.measured: Fragments None and 'c1' raised AttributeError, index '0' raised TypeError and index -1 raised IndexError, each answered as error_code internal; each is now skipped and the usable call in the same stream is returned.

issues.title: A streamed tool-call index has no upper bound
issues.description: The buffer that assembles streamed tool calls grows to the index a fragment names, appending an empty slot for each position, so one short fragment from the upstream can allocate millions of slots. Same class as bug-005 and bug-006 (no bound on what the upstream makes this process hold). Bounding it needs a decision on the largest index to accept and on whether a fragment past it fails the answer or is dropped.
issues.measured: One fragment with index 5,000,000 raised peak traced memory to 347 MiB and took 15 s under tracemalloc before the answer returned.
